title: Ephemeral Port Pressure Mitigation and Proxy Pooling Playbook (Draft)
body:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a pragmatic approach to reducing ephemeral port exhaustion and improving tenant isolation for private/VPC inference deployments. It focuses on two complementary strategies: per-tenant proxy pools (sidecar or shared edge proxies) and SNAT/session scaling patterns (port re-use, EPHEMERAL range tuning, and backend connection pooling). Goal is to provide step-by-step Terraform notes, a migration plan, and incident mitigations for teams running Redwood Private in customer VPCs or on-prem clusters.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Kubernetes-based private deployments (K8s clusters hosting inference pods and edge proxies) and appliance-based on-prem nodes that use NAT for outbound traffic.
- Customers use a mix of host-NAT and cloud NAT gateways; we assume we can deploy additional proxy replicas.
- Doesn't cover deep L7 auth or application-layer routing beyond proxy behavior.

Background / Problem statement:
- Observed customer incidents where a surge of short-lived inference requests from many pods caused ephemeral port exhaustion on SNAT devices, resulting in 502s or TCP resets.
- Root causes typically: large fanout, short client socket lifetimes, aggressive client-side concurrency, and conservative ephemeral port ranges on customer NAT boxes.
- Secondary problem: tenant traffic intermixing leads to noisy neighbor performance and harder audit trails.

High-level approach:
1) Reduce amount of distinct source tuples hitting SNAT by routing outbound requests through per-tenant proxy pools with connection reuse (keepalive).
2) Increase SNAT headroom via ephemeral port tuning and using multiple SNAT IPs or pool-based SNAT (where supported).
3) Apply conservative client-side connection pooling and retry/backoff to reduce churn.
4) Provide Terraform-managed IP allocation and routing artifacts for predictable deployment.

Architecture sketch (two modes):
- Shared-edge-proxy mode (default for small customers): a small set of regional proxy replicas (daemonset/static pools) with sticky source IPs. Each tenant routes through a tenant-aware proxy pool via iptables or CNI egress rules.
- Sidecar-consolidation mode (default for high-isolation customers): sidecar proxies are attached per-pod but use a shared upstream connection pool process (local proxy aggregator) to reduce connection fanout to SNAT devices.

Terraform module notes (practical details):
- module name: private-network/proxy-pool
  - variables: tenant_id (string), region (string), desired_replicas (number), allowed_egress_ports (list), allocate_static_eips (bool default false), nat_ip_count (number default 0)
  - outputs: proxy_public_ips (list), proxy_internal_dns (string), proxy_asg_name (string)
- module design decisions: prefer idempotent resources and explicit IP allocation for dedicated proxies. If allocate_static_eips=true, module will create reserved IPs and attach to proxies to keep SNAT source addresses stable across scale events.
- SRV/DNS records: create per-tenant CNAME entries in the customer's private DNS zone (Terraform aws_route53_record / gcp_dns_record) for proxy discovery. Use short TTLs (30s) only during rollout, then increase to 300s after stabilization.
- Network policy templates: Provide a module to generate Kubernetes NetworkPolicies that pin workloads to egress targets using namespace/label selectors rather than IPs (simpler for terraform-managed overlays).
- Migration helper: terraform resource aws_lb_target_group with health checks to gracefully drain proxy replicas; topic: include lifecycle.prevent_destroy for critical IP allocations during early phases.

Operational runbook (quick triage):
Symptoms:
- Sudden spike in 502/504 to external services from inference pods
- NAT gateway logs show port exhaustion errors or high TIME_WAIT churn
- Customer complains about intermittent outbound failures after scale-up

Immediate mitigation steps:
1) Gradually reduce client concurrency by setting per-worker concurrency limit to 8 (if default is higher).
2) Redirect a subset of tenants to a cold standby proxy pool that has reserved IPs. Terraform step: set allocate_static_eips=true for that tenant and apply.
3) If using cloud NAT: increase NAT ports per-second limits or add additional NAT IPs via the console/TF patch (quick patch: set nat_ip_count +=1).
4) Enable connection reuse on HTTP clients (keepalive and large connection pool) and increase keepalive timeout to 60s.

Testing checklist (pre-rollout):
- Unit: verify the proxy module creates the expected number of EIPs and records in a sandbox account.
- Integration: run a synthetic fanout test (1000 short-lived connections/min) and assert no 502s and no NAT port exhaustion over 10 minutes.
- Chaos: simulate a probe that kills 50% of proxy replicas and confirm target group drains without packets lost for >95% of requests.
- Metrics: add dashboards that show ephemeral port utilization, SNAT source IP diversity, pod connection counts, and per-tenant P95 external request latency.

Staged migration plan:
Phase 0: Canary (1–2 tenants)
- Deploy proxy-pool module with allocate_static_eips=false, small replica count, instrument metrics, and run synthetic load.
- Verify connection reuse reduces SNAT port counts by >40%.
Phase 1: Regional rollout
- For tenants with observed pressure, enable allocate_static_eips=true and bump replicas.
- Adjust firewall rules to allow proxy IP ranges outbound.
Phase 2: Full enforcement + cleanup
- Convert remaining tenants to route via proxy pools and deprecate client-side direct egress rules.
- Remove old iptables rules and nonmanaged NAT hacks.

Backward compatibility notes:
- Preserve an opt-out label (networking.redwood.io/egress=direct) for legacy customers for at least 90 days post-rollout.
- Make health endpoints and metrics available at /healthz and /metrics on proxy for monitoring.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Offline/on-prem NAT boxes: do we ship a tiny NAT appliance image to provide deterministic ephemeral port ranges for air-gapped customers? (marketing + legal input required)
- Audit: how do we link per-tenant logs to customer audit trails when proxies pool traffic? Add tenant-id headers at proxy and retain downstream traces.
- Terraform idempotency for IP reuse across environments (edge case: IPs accidentally destroyed during infra drift) — consider a lifecycle rule and pre-check hook.

Notes for SRE and Solutions Eng (quick tips):
- When triaging, always check last 24h SNAT port histogram (Cloud NAT / onprem NAT logs).
- If ephemeral ports are nearly saturated and you cannot add IPs, prefer reducing connection churn over increasing NAT capacity; connection reuse yields much larger gains.
- Track tenant-level p99 latency before and after proxy rollout — some tenants may see small increases due to an extra hop; balance via colocating proxies in same subnet/zone.

References and helpful links:
- RFC about ephemeral port reuse and TIME_WAIT behavior (internal link)
- GitHub PR with initial terraform module: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/118
- JIRA-INF-3421: incident for customer X (root cause: SNAT port exhaustion)

Status / next steps:
- This is a working draft. Action items: 1) merge Terraform module MVP (Benji), 2) synthetic load harness for onprem customers (Marta), 3) draft customer migration emails + opt-out process (Devon).

Quick checklist (TL;DR):
- [ ] Add proxy-pool module to infra repo and test in sandbox
- [ ] Create per-tenant DNS records and healthcheck TGs
- [ ] Run synthetic fanout test and validate metrics
- [ ] Prepare customer communication + opt-out window

Notes to self: keep the TTL conservative during rollout, prefer 60–300s. Avoid automatic IP reallocation on destroy until customers have migrated.

End of draft.
